This 2015 Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Has Only 1,259 Miles, Care To Buy It?
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks
Is it wrong that some of us still dream about owning a Hellcat ? After all, this model hasn’t been a thing for a few years now, because production of the third-gen Dodge Challenger ended in 2023, after 15 years.
That is also when its four-door sibling, the seventh-gen Charger, was put to sleep, and as everyone and their pet knows, Dodge’s new-age muscle car uses this moniker. The eighth-gen will blow two candles off its birthday cake next month (December 2024). It is made in Canada, and comes either win a twin-turbocharged straight-six engine or with battery-electric power.
However, the V8-powered model is reportedly in the making as Dodge’s way of saying “we’re sorry,” and word on the street is that it could come out at the end of 2027 as a 2028 model year car. That’s roughly one year from now, but the wait should be worth it, because it seems that the Hellcat might be the engine of choice. And if the rumors are correct, then both body styles, the two-door coupe and the four-door sedan, will get the supercharged V8 mill.
It remains to be seen whether it will have the same 6.2-liter displacement as the demised Hellcat versions of the old Dodge Challenger and Charger, as well as the Jeep Grand Cherokee Trackhawk. And speaking of this unit, it is not dead, because it lives on in the Durango and the Ram 1500 SRT TRX.
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks If we were to bet on it, we’d say that it might be an updated version of the 6.2-liter supercharged V8, perhaps with over 800 horsepower. At first, that is, because chances are the company will eventually expand the lineup with all sort of hot muscle cars, and right before pulling the plug on the current Charger, it is possible that Dodge might launch a proper successor to the Challenger SRT Demon 170 .
The latter remains the world’s fastest and most powerful production muscle car to date. It has up to 1,025 horsepower and 945 pound-feet (1,280 Nm) of torque in its top configuration, hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in 1.66 seconds, and running the standing 1/4-mile in 8.91 seconds, at 151.17 mph (243.28 kph). That’s faster than the new Chevy Corvette ZR1X, if you are keeping track of these things.
Now, the muscle car pictured in the gallery is far from being a Demon, let alone a Demon 170, as we are looking at a regular Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat from the 2015 model year. This means that it has 707 horsepower available via the right pedal, channeled to the rear axle through a six-speed manual transmission in this case.
Therefore, the driver engagement factor is definitely there, and interested parties should know that this machine has only 1,259 miles (2,026 km). Thus, it is pretty much brand new. Some of the goodies mentioned in the listing include the Redline Red Tri-Coat Pearl exterior paint finish, black leather interior, Customer Preferred Package 25R, Premium Laguna Leather SRT seats, Harman Kardon premium sound system, and a dual-zone climate control system.
Moreover, this Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat also features HID headlights, an SRT Performance spoiler, a limited-slip differential, 9.5x20-inch wheels, Brembo brakes with red calipers, HID Air-Catcher headlamps, an SRT-tuned Bilstein suspension, parking sensors at the rear, and black vapor chrome exhaust tips, among other things.
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks According to the vendor, which is known as @diamondmotorworks on Instagram, the muscle car in question is offered with two keys, the usual lecture, and a set of floor mats, among other things. The vehicle is in stock and waiting for you to make a move. And before revealing the asking price, we have to tell you that these things do not tend to brake the bank at all.
In fact, one must fork out between $25,000 and some $55,000 for a 2015 model year Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat in today’s used car market in the United States of America. Cars with less than 30,000 miles (48,000 km) on the clock tend to be pricier, whereas those that approach a six-digit mileage are found at the lower end of the spectrum price-wise.
So, how much do you think the pictured 2015 Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat costs? Well, given that it has extremely low mileage, and that it packs plenty of goodies, you already know that it will set you back more than the average muscle car in this configuration, from this model year, don’t you? Without any further ado, you will have to cough out $61,800 if you want to write your name on the dotted line.
Is it worth the asking price? Well, it is if you want a new Hellcat from the 2015 model year, which looks as good today as it did when it initially left the dealership, and if you must really have this one, then you know what to do next, don’t you? But realistically speaking, would you pay almost $62K for and old Dodge? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Diamond Motorworks (@diamondmotorworks)
